result.summary: Verdict FINDINGS (2 x LOW, no CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM) at target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 on branch feature/binary-config-serve-20260930. Scope: SIGTERM/SIGINT and repeated stop, outstanding coordinator operations, shutdown deadline, SQLite close races. F1 (LOW, reproduced): in-flight read-only MCP tool calls hit a closed SQLite after the drain - release() closes the store after awaiting only Coordinator-tracked work, while WorkerFiles handlers (src/files.ts:121,142) and the lazy redactor (src/security.ts:48 via src/mcp.ts:40 and the catch at src/mcp.ts:60) are untracked, raising RangeError: Cannot use a closed database; 0 post-close writes, 0 unhandled rejections. F2 (LOW, code-evidenced): a repeated signal is dropped at src/serve-command.ts:112, so a stuck drain always runs the full 60s default deadline and exits 70; with systemd TimeoutStopSec below that the unit is SIGKILLed (137). The core drain was found sound: all store writes are either inside Coordinator.track() or fully synchronous, Coordinator.stop() cannot reject, and release()'s try/finally cannot be skipped. Tests: bun 1.4.2 (installed under /tmp, lockfile untouched); bun test tests/serve.test.ts 20 pass / 0 fail; two reviewer probes in /tmp/rv-probe exit 0. Report: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json.
result.details:
Reviewed src/serve-command.ts, src/serve.ts, src/coordinator.ts, src/store.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/http.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/files.ts, src/security.ts, src/main.ts, docs/SERVE.md, tests/serve.test.ts, tests/fixtures/serve-command-child.ts.

F1 LOW, src/serve.ts:152 trigger. Un-drained readers run against a closed database: WorkerFiles.get_worker_logs re-reads the store after an await on provider.getWorker (src/files.ts:121) and again at src/files.ts:142; artifact and swarmforge:// resource reads share the shape; redactorFor evaluates c.store.all() lazily on every string (src/security.ts:48) so it is reached by the MCP response path (src/mcp.ts:40) and by the tool error path (src/mcp.ts:60). The second site is inside register()'s catch, so the handler's own error path throws and no isError result is produced. Contained: no unhandled rejection, no crash, no post-close writes (POST-CLOSE WRITES 0 in both probes). Why guards miss it: docs/SERVE.md and tests/serve.test.ts:643 cover only wait_for_state_change, which stopWaiters does wake. Fix: make Store.close() set a closed flag and have read methods return a neutral result, and/or track WorkerFiles handlers and snapshot the redactor secret set once.

F2 LOW, src/serve-command.ts:112. onSignal returns on any repeat and the deadline timer is created only on the first signal, so repeated Ctrl-C cannot escalate; a drain blocked on a non-settling provider promise or on pushBranch (SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS default 120000, src/config.ts:53, which already exceeds the 60s shutdown deadline) always runs to the deadline and exits 70. Deliberate and asserted by tests/serve.test.ts:835. Fix: escalate on a second signal to a short grace deadline or exit 70.

Verified non-findings (traced, not reported as defects): Coordinator.control()'s trailing store.get at src/coordinator.ts:814 sits outside track(), but track's finally resolves idle before stop()'s while-loop continuation is queued, so control's continuation runs before store.close(); the abort registration window at src/serve.ts:199-205 is synchronous so no signal callback can run inside it and runServe's if (requested) re-check covers the rest; Coordinator.stop() is structurally incapable of rejecting so release()'s trailing flush/close/unlock cannot be skipped; the poll interval keeps firing between gate.close() and coordinator.stop() but stop() awaits the resulting tracked tick; no post-close write is reachable since spawn/message are synchronous end to end and every other write is inside track().

Reproducibility: probes live only at /tmp/rv-probe/probe-postclose.ts and /tmp/rv-probe/probe2.ts, outside the source checkout, and patch Store.prototype at runtime; no source file was modified and nothing was committed. All provider/agent calls used the repo's FakeProvider/FakeAgent against a throwaway SQLite file in mkdtemp on loopback ports; no real cloud, model provider or infrastructure was contacted. The system bun is 1.3.14 and cannot read this lockfileVersion 2, so official Bun 1.4.2 was installed at /tmp/bun142 and the lockfile was never rewritten. No whole-suite run and no compile, both out of scope for this reviewer. Artifact reads for get_worker_artifact and the resource template were inferred from the same code path as get_worker_logs rather than probed separately. No credentials, .env files or secret stores were inspected.

result.followup_reason: Two actionable LOW findings in the serve/shutdown scope. F1 (src/serve.ts:152 trigger; untracked readers at src/files.ts:121,142 and src/security.ts:48 via src/mcp.ts:40,60): make Store.close() safe for late readers and/or track WorkerFiles handlers plus snapshot the redactor secret set, so a shutdown does not raise RangeError: Cannot use a closed database inside an in-flight tool call. F2 (src/serve-command.ts:112): let a repeated signal escalate to a short grace deadline instead of always waiting the full SWARMFORGE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS and exiting 70, which is SIGKILLed as 137 under a shorter systemd TimeoutStopSec. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM issue was found: all store writes are either inside Coordinator.track() or fully synchronous, Coordinator.stop() cannot reject, and release()'s trailing flush/close/unlock cannot be skipped.
